pageCache.text:
Headteacher
Edith Kerrison Nursery School and Children’s Centre will work together with you to give your child the best start in life through nurturing their well-being and enabling them to become confident, creative and resilient learners.
We are located in Custom House where we have been established as a state-maintained nursery school for over 90 years and our Children’s Centre is the lead centre for Custom House and Canning Town. Some of our families bring East End traditions to Edith Kerrison, whilst others bring global experiences. We believe together we are a stronger community.
We have a talented multi-disciplinary team of teachers, educators, outreach and family support workers to help our community on its learning journey. We work in partnership with other professionals including speech therapists, health visitors, nutritionists, special needs workers and return-to-work officers.
We want to make a difference together to ensure your child’s time here is a happy and successful one.
Best wishes Jo Aylett

pageCache.text:
Nurturing confident learners from the very start
At Edith Kerrison Nursery School and Children’s Centre, we believe early childhood is a time to feel safe, to explore freely, and to be truly known.
We are more than just a nursery – we’re a caring community that sees each child as unique, capable and full of potential.
A Place Where Children Flourish
Our aim is simple: to give every child the best possible start in life. Whether it’s their first experience of education or a step on their journey, we work together to build strong foundations for life-long learning by supporting children’s emotional well-being, communication, creativity and independence.
Our Approach
At the heart of our practice is a child-centered approach. We follow each child’s interests, supporting their curiosity and confidence through meaningful play, real-life experiences, and skilled adult guidance.
We know that children learn best when they feel secure and valued. That’s why relationships come first. Our experienced team builds warm, trusting connections with every child – helping them feel safe, seen, and ready to learn.
Vision Statement
Together we Play, Talk, Listen and Learn
WE PLAY in ways that provide opportunities for exploration, creativity, thinking and challenge.
WE TALK to communicate and express our thoughts, ideas and feelings.
WE LISTEN attentively to others’ ideas and views, enjoying learning and responding to our world.
WE LEARN by persevering; we are aspirational; we empower and develop ourselves and community.
What Makes Us Special?
“Children are happy, safe and motivated to learn” – Ofsted.
We are proud of our most recent Ofsted report, which recognised that:
“Staff have high expectations for what children can achieve”
“Children behave well. They are kind, confident and respectful.”
“The curriculum is ambitious and thoughtfully designed.”
“Children make strong progress and are well prepared for their next stage of learning.”
Caring, Experienced Team
Our staff are passionate early year’s educators who build meaningful relationships and tailor support to each child’s needs.
Emotionally Supportive Environment
We help children name and manage their feelings, develop empathy, and build friendships – with a strong focus on mental health and well-being.
Inclusive and welcoming
Every child and every family is valued here. We embrace diversity and adapt our practice so that every learner can thrive.
Beautiful Learning Spaces
Our indoor and outdoor environments are designed to inspire curiosity, independence and creativity. We spend time outside everyday – rain or shine!
Movement for Healthy Bodies and Minds
Physical development is a vital part of our curriculum. Children climb, run, balance, dig, dance and explore freely – building strong, healthy bodies and coordination. Through movement, they also learn focus, confidence, and joy in being active.
A Strong Focus on Communication
Supporting language development is a central part of our work. We create a language-rich environment where children are listened to, encouraged to express themselves, and introduced to a wide vocabulary through stories, songs, conversation, and play. We also work closely with speech and language professionals to ensure any concerns are addressed early and effectively.
Strong Family Partnerships
We work closely with parents and carers because we know children learn best when we’re working together. Your voice matters, and your child’s journey is shared.
Edith Kerrison is a truly communication-friendly setting. Staff are highly skilled at tuning in to children’s needs and supporting speech and language development from the earliest stages. Whether a child is developing typically or needs targeted support, they are given the time, attention, and tools to succeed.”
Getting Ready for what’s Next
As children grow with us, we gently guide them towards greater independence, confidence and school readiness.
We build strong foundations for lifelong learning – socially, emotionally, and academically – so that children leave us prepared and excited for primary school.
WE’D LOVE TO WELCOME YOU TO EDITH KERRISON
Come and see our nursery in action, meet our wonderful team, and find out how we can support your child to thrive.
Book a visit Read our Full Ofsted report Meet the Team
Core Services
We are the main centre for Custom House and Canning Town, offering the Best Start in Life initiative.
Our services are accompanied by a listening ear and kindness, which we believe are the foundations of meaningful and professional relationships.
We also guide families to other professional support, such as speech therapists and psychologists.

The Nursery School and Children’s Centre are led by a senior team including the Headteacher, Assistant Headteacher, Children’s Centre Manager, and Business Manager.
The strategic direction is decided with input from the Governing Body, mostly comprised of local community residents.
Additional staff are available for projects and individual child support, along with part-time specialists including a speech and language therapist, dance therapist, music teacher, and a football coach.

Admissions at a glance
The admissions process for children aged two, three, and four can be initiated at the reception of Edith Kerrison Nursery School and Children’s Centre.
If you are looking for a nursery place for your child, please register at the school reception. Download our Registration Form.
The information about childcare and education options is provided by Newham Council.
When can my child start nursery?

2 Year old places
Children who are two years old are usually offered a place to start after they turn two. Two-year-olds must attend some children’s centre sessions and may have a home visit. If there are no available places, you can put your child’s name on our waiting list or register them with other childcare providers.
Am I eligible for 15 hours?
3 & 4 year old places
Children three years old are usually allowed to start the term after their third birthday. Before the starting date, they must attend pre-school play sessions with their parent. During these sessions, parents have the chance to meet with the Head Teacher. At least one parent must attend one of these sessions before a starting date is offered.
Universal 15 hours entitlement
30 hour week
Did you know the 15-hour placements have expanded?
We provide 30-hour placements for up to 18 eligible families. Priority is given to children who have accepted a 15-hour placement. The Department for Education establishes the criteria for eligibility.

A Message from
the Governing Body
At Edith Kerrison, we believe that every child deserves the highest quality start to their educational journey. As the Governing Body, our primary role is to provide strategic leadership and ensure that the school and children’s centre remain a safe, nurturing, and ambitious environment for our entire community.
Our governors come from a diverse range of backgrounds. They include parents, staff, and members of the local community, all bringing a wealth of experience to our shared mission.
How we work
We are incredibly proud of the vibrant, inclusive, and joyful atmosphere at Edith Kerrison. Together, we strive to build a foundation where children feel confident to explore, learn, and grow.
We work closely with the Headteacher and the Senior Leadership Team to:
UPHOLD EXCELLENCE We monitor the quality of teaching and learning to ensure every child makes outstanding progress.
ENSURE ACCOUNTABILITY We oversee the school’s financial health and ensure resources are used effectively to benefit the children.
FOSTER WELLBEING We are committed to a “whole-child” approach, supporting the physical, emotional, and social development of every family that walks through our doors.
Interested in joining us?
Being a governor is a rewarding way to give back to the community and help shape the future of our children. We welcome individuals who are passionate about early years education and are willing to contribute their time and skills.
Financial Information
Financial Information
Schools are required to publish the number of employees whose gross annual salary exceeds £100,000. This information must be presented in £10,000 bandings.
As of the current academic year, no employees at our school earn a gross annual salary of £100,000 or more.

THE GREEN ROOM
The rhythm of our school day
We know children learn best when secure, confident and actively engaged. We believe that young children learn best when their education is driven by their interests and fascinations, and through play and exploration.
Morning
8.40am - The children arrive for the morning session
Children find their name card and badge and parents are encouraged to help their child pick a book from our library. Children are welcomed by staff in the classroom. Our environment allows children to choose their activities indoors and outdoors based on their interests. Activities focus on communication, language, physical development, social and emotional well-being, art, music, science, mathematics, and literacy. Adults ensure children have time and freedom to engage in play and practice their skills.
9.30 / 10:30 - Preparation of Snacks
Children can choose from a variety of fruits, vegetables, water, and milk, which they help prepare.
11:35 - The learning experiences continue until collection
The learning experiences continue until the children come together for a story, songs, and rhymes. Afterwards, they either go home or stay for lunch. The doors open at this time for collection.
Afternoon
12:30 - The children arrive for the afternoon session
Children find their name card and badge and parents are encouraged to help their child pick a book from our library. Children are welcomed by staff in the classroom. Our environment allows children to choose their activities indoors and outdoors based on their interests. Activities focus on communication, language, physical development, social and emotional well-being, art, music, science, mathematics, and literacy. Adults ensure children have time and freedom to engage in play and practice their skills.
13.00 / 14:00 - Preparation of Snacks
Children can choose from a variety of fruits, vegetables, water, and milk, which they help prepare.
15:25 - The learning experiences continue until collection
The learning experiences continue until the children come together for a story, songs, and rhymes. The doors open at this time for collection.
Full Time children attending for 30 hours
The routine continues for all our children, including those who are full-time. The significant difference is that our full-time children will have their lunch from 11:40 am to 12:25 pm. Children attending for 30 hours are collected at 14:40.

Children's Centre
Welcome
Edith Kerrison Children’s Centre has a dedicated team to support families in the local community. Our team consists of a Centre Coordinator, Senior Practitioners, Senior Family Support Workers, Family Support Workers, and Early Years practitioners.
We aim to create a warm, welcoming, and inclusive environment. Our goal is to collaborate with families and children to provide the best start in life.
We are the lead centre providing services to families in Custom House and Canning Town. Our services are run in partnership with Keir Hardie Primary School.
Children's Centre
Welcome
Edith Kerrison Children’s Centre has a dedicated team to support families in the local community. Our team consists of a Centre Coordinator, Senior Practitioners, Senior Family Support Workers, Family Support Workers, and Early Years practitioners.
We aim to create a warm, welcoming, and inclusive environment. Our goal is to collaborate with families and children to provide the best start in life.
We are the lead centre providing services to families in Custom House and Canning Town. Our services are run in partnership with Keir Hardie Primary School.
Universal services
Drop-in sessions do not require booking. Our universal services include baby and toddler groups, messy play, and storytime. These services are quite popular, so we kindly ask that you arrive no more than 10 minutes before the session starts. It’s important to be aware that some sessions have limited capacity. In the winter, in particular, it may not be possible to attend if we are full, and we may have to close registration due to health and safety reasons.
Targeted services
We offer a wide range of services. Universal services are open to all but have limited capacity and become booked quickly. Other health services can be accessed through drop-ins, such as oral health promotion. Some services are provided by children’s centre staff, such as Baby Massage and Stop the Bottle. These may also require booking. It is important to check the Activity Programme to see whether you need to book a session. We also signpost to support groups such as breastfeeding.
Multi-Professional Partnerships
The Children’s Centre collaborates with various professionals to offer a wide range of services and developmental play for children with complex needs. This collaboration includes speech and language therapists, health visitors, educational advisors, and other practitioners.
Two year old provision
We offer education and care for all eligible two-year-olds, with a place available through government funding. The government has set the criteria for accessing this free place. Learn more about Two Year Old Provision
3 hours a day
We offer a 3-hour morning or afternoon program, available every weekday during term time. Consistent attendance is important for your child to make the best progress. We value collaboration with all parents and carers.
Workshops
Workshops and events are an excellent way to connect with other parents and exchange parenting ideas. You can gain insight into your child’s learning both at home and in school. Our workshops and parent events are very popular.
Our opening times
The Children’s Centre has a dedicated team to support families in the local community. During the sessions, you will meet either family support or outreach workers. These sessions offer informal opportunities to discuss pregnancy, babies, children, and family life.
Entrance The entrance is via Canning Town Recreation Park. You can get there by following the directions via Sophia Road park entrance. Once you’re at the park, follow the perimeter of the school and then follow the pathway. When you pass the tennis courts, take the pathway to the right. You will find the entrance gate, which has a Children’s Centre sign, located along the fence.
The staff at the children’s centre are available at the following times:
Opening Hours Monday to Friday 8.00 am to 4.00 pm Closed for Bank Holidays
At other times please call 0207 476 1735
Registration
Registration can be completed online via the Best Start in Life Registration Form.
If you don’t have a card or have recently moved to the area, please visit the centre, and we will register you in our system. You don’t need to bring any documents, and you can start using our services on the same day as your registration. Our services are free.

Booking
Please call the central booking line for sessions that require booking, unless stated differently. Please call the day before to book a place. Please call on a Friday to book a Monday group.
Booking times are 9am – 3pm Central booking number 0207 473 2761
Transparency
All service users will have access to 3 groups per week, based on the age of the child, at both sites. Families receiving support through our services will be able to access additional sessions. If sessions are full, a waiting list will be in place. For more information, please call and speak to a member of the team, or register here for Newham BSiL Children’s Centres
Our programme can change and due to limited capacity, only one adult per family is admitted to a group unless otherwise arranged.
Please note that not all activities are held at the Children’s Centre. some are held at Family Hub Shipman Youth Zone. Please refer to our Activity Programme for details.
Gain exclusive access to a wide array of enriching activities, programs, and resources at any Children’s Centre in Newham.
Family Support
Life can be challenging, and we sometimes need support to navigate difficult situations. Our team of experienced family support workers is able to offer you help during times of worries and concerns, no matter how small it may seem.
Please contact the centre to speak to a family support worker. They can offer support with signposting to the food bank, SEND, domestic abuse organisations, parenting support, child development, emotional well-being, and much more.
Childcare
If you require childcare, please visit Newham Family Information Service. Childminders are able to offer 15-30 hours of childcare.
Healthy Start
Vitamins
Edith Kerrison Children’s Centre is a distribution centre for Healthy Start Vitamins
All pregnant women, new mothers, and children under the age of 4 can access free vitamins, including the recommended amount of Vitamin D, in Newham.
Collection times: 9am-3pm Monday to Friday
Infant Feeding Team
Support
Our Infant Feeding Team are skilled and experienced specialists here to support you with breastfeeding, bottle feeding, mixed feeding, and much more.
For 1-1 help 7 days a week via Newham Baby Feeding Helpline 07534 249611 or [email protected]
Baby Feeding Cafés
Mondays and Fridays
Meet the team at our friendly Baby Feeding Cafés. For more information see our events for Baby Feeding Café.
Newham Breastfeeding Welcome – you can breastfeed your baby everywhere in Newham – you’re protected by law. Look out for our Breastfeeding Welcome logo and sticker.

Edith Kerrison Children’s Centre is a distribution centre for Healthy Start Vitamins
All pregnant women, new mothers, and children under the age of 4 can access free vitamins, including the recommended amount of Vitamin D, in Newham. Collection times: 9am-3pm Monday to Friday, Term time only
At other times, please call 0207 476 1735

The Nursery School
Together we Play, Talk, Listen and Learn
Edith Kerrison Nursery School has served Custom House and Canning Town for over 90 years. Explore our historic setting at the heart of the community.
Inspired by the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) framework, our curriculum focuses on the holistic development of each child, encompassing their social, emotional, physical, and cognitive growth. Through structured activities and free play, we aim to foster independence, creativity, and a love for learning in every child.
The Classrooms
Where young minds blossom and grow
At Edith Kerrison our classrooms are designed to provide a nurturing environment for young children to learn, blossom and grow. From the cozy “Snuggery” for 2-year-olds to the vibrant Blue, Red, and Green classrooms for 3-4 year-olds, each space is designed to support their developmental journey. All the rooms consists of a teacher and early years educators.
Curriculum Overview
We know children learn best when secure, confident and actively engaged. We believe that young children learn best when their education is driven by their interests and fascinations, and through play and exploration.
We focus on providing the right environment for children to learn and grow, ensuring that all children, including those with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), are included and supported in our curriculum.
5 Key Elements
1 Teaching and learning based on children’s interests
2 Learning related to core books, songs and rhymes
3 Nature, connecting with seasons and natural world
4 Educational visits and visitors
5 Core experiences: dance and movement
Curriculum in Focus
Our staff cover all seven areas of learning outlined in the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage 2021. Development Matters and OPAL milestones inform us what children need to know to progress through the curriculum.
You can also attend our workshops for parents, see ‘Workshop for Parents’ in Key Documentation / Miscellaneous.

THE BLUE ROOM
The rhythm of our school day
We know children learn best when secure, confident and actively engaged. We believe that young children learn best when their education is driven by their interests and fascinations, and through play and exploration.
Morning
8.40am - The children arrive for the morning session
Children find their name card and badge and parents are encouraged to help their child pick a book from our library. Children are welcomed by staff in the classroom. Our environment allows children to choose their activities indoors and outdoors based on their interests. Activities focus on communication, language, physical development, social and emotional well-being, art, music, science, mathematics, and literacy. Adults ensure children have time and freedom to engage in play and practice their skills.
9.30 / 10:30 - Preparation of Snacks
Children can choose from a variety of fruits, vegetables, water, and milk, which they help prepare.
11:35 - The learning experiences continue until collection
The learning experiences continue until the children come together for a story, songs, and rhymes. Afterwards, they either go home or stay for lunch. The doors open at this time for collection.
Afternoon
12:30 - The children arrive for the afternoon session
Children find their name card and badge and parents are encouraged to help their child pick a book from our library. Children are welcomed by staff in the classroom. Our environment allows children to choose their activities indoors and outdoors based on their interests. Activities focus on communication, language, physical development, social and emotional well-being, art, music, science, mathematics, and literacy. Adults ensure children have time and freedom to engage in play and practice their skills.
13.00 / 14:00 - Preparation of Snacks
Children can choose from a variety of fruits, vegetables, water, and milk, which they help prepare.
15:25 - The learning experiences continue until collection
The learning experiences continue until the children come together for a story, songs, and rhymes. The doors open at this time for collection.
Full Time children attending for 30 hours
The routine continues for all our children, including those who are full-time. The significant difference is that our full-time children will have their lunch from 11:40 am to 12:25 pm. Children attending for 30 hours are collected at 14:40.
